definitions.definition: Space = Fin n → ℝ, the fixed standard coordinates on ℝⁿ, with its product norm, Borel structure and topology.
Value = Fin m → ℝ, the fixed standard coordinates on ℝᵐ, with its product norm and topology.
For v,w∈Value, dot(v,w)=∑_{k∈Fin m} v(k)w(k). This is the Euclidean dot product.
For v∈Value, normSq(v)=dot(v,v), the Euclidean norm squared.
In the fixed standard coordinates, ubar(x,t)=u(x,t) for t>0 and ubar(x,t)=q for t≤0. This is a total representative only; its definition asserts no regularity at t=0.

definitions.type: open-domain notation: subset of Space × ℝ
definitions.definition: U={(x,t)∈Space×ℝ:0<t}. All calculus assertions about ubar are restricted to U.
For j∈Fin n, basis(j)=Pi.single j 1 is the standard vector with coordinate 1 at j and 0 elsewhere.

definitions.type: notation for calculus, topology and measure
definitions.definition: AnalyticNotation fixes the following typed conventions, with each function, space, point and measure supplied by its own statement or local scope. D and fderiv denote the Fréchet derivative over the field specified at each use, defaulting to ℝ; deriv is the corresponding one-variable derivative. The total derivative operators return zero when a derivative does not exist. HasDerivAt relates a one-variable function, its derivative value and its basepoint. ContDiffOn and ContDiffAt express the indicated C-order regularity on a set or at a point; ∞ means all finite orders and ω means analytic. minSmoothness at order 2 is 2 for a field satisfying IsRCLikeNormedField and ω otherwise; IsSymmSndFDerivAt means that the second Fréchet derivative at the specified point is symmetric in its two direction arguments. 𝓝 denotes the neighborhood filter. The support of a function is the set where its value is nonzero, tsupport is the closure of that set, and HasCompactSupport means this closure is compact. ContinuousOn means continuity relative to the indicated set. AEStronglyMeasurable means agreement almost everywhere with a strongly measurable function. Integrable means ae strong measurability and finite integral of the norm; IntegrableOn means integrability with respect to the restriction of the specified measure to the specified set. The Bochner integral uses the total library convention; for real integrable functions it is the ordinary finite Lebesgue integral. A set indicator equals its function on that set and zero off it. An ae assertion holds outside a null set for the indicated measure. The extended norm on an ESeminormedAddMonoid is denoted by ‖·‖ₑ; real numbers have finite extended norm. Standard structure names retain their usual mathematical meanings: OpensMeasurableSpace says that open sets are measurable, BorelSpace identifies the measurable structure with the Borel structure, IsFiniteMeasureOnCompacts says compact sets have finite measure, and IsAddHaarMeasure means an additive Haar measure. These conventions define notation and assert no application theorem.
V(x,t)_k=deriv (r↦ubar(x,r)_k) t, for each x,t and k∈Fin m.
L(x,t)=∑_{j∈Fin n} Ssp(j,x,t), the componentwise spatial Laplacian.

dx is canonical Lebesgue volume on Space: the product of the usual real Lebesgue measures in its fixed standard coordinates. It is the original dx on ℝⁿ. Spatial integrals without a displayed measure use dx.
e(x,t)=normSq(V(x,t))+∑_{j∈Fin n} normSq(Psp(j,x,t)). This is |u_t|²+∑_j |∂_{x_j}u|² at positive times, with the Euclidean/Frobenius squares and coefficient 1 on each term.
E(t)=∫_{Space} e(x,t) dx, using the total integral convention until integrability is proved. At positive times when integrable this is the original finite energy integral.

inputs.statement: For every x∈ℝⁿ and t>0, |u(x,t)|=1 for the Euclidean norm.
For every x∈ℝⁿ and t>0 there exists a real scalar a such that u_tt(x,t)−Δ_x u(x,t)=a u(x,t), with Δ_x u=∑_{j=1}^n ∂_{x_jx_j}u componentwise. No regularity or global choice of the scalar is assumed.

The fixed standard-coordinate representation Space=Fin n→ℝ and Value=Fin m→ℝ identifies the original Euclidean map with ubar restricted to U; Euclidean squares are normSq and the original dx is the product Lebesgue volume dx with no scaling. At positive times V=u_t, A=u_tt, Psp(j)=∂_j u, Ssp(j)=∂_jj u, L=Δ_xu, e=|u_t|²+∑_j|∂_j u|² and E is the same total integral expression, finite whenever e is integrable. The fields ubar,V,A,Psp(j),Ssp(j),W(j),e,d are C∞ on U for every j∈Fin n. For every x∈Space, t>0, k∈Fin m and j∈Fin n: HasDerivAt (r↦ubar(x,r)_k) V(x,t)_k t; HasDerivAt (r↦V(x,r)_k) A(x,t)_k t; HasDerivAt (r↦Psp(j,x,r)_k) W(j,x,t)_k t; fderiv ℝ (y↦ubar(y,t)_k) x (basis(j))=Psp(j,x,t)_k; fderiv ℝ (y↦V(y,t)_k) x (basis(j))=W(j,x,t)_k; and fderiv ℝ (y↦Psp(j,y,t)_k) x (basis(j))=Ssp(j,x,t)_k. In particular the time derivative of Psp(j) and the spatial j derivative of V coincide. Moreover HasDerivAt (r↦e(x,r)) d(x,t) t, with d(x,t)=2 dot(V(x,t),A(x,t))+2∑_j dot(Psp(j,x,t),W(j,x,t)). No assertion of regularity across zero is made.

For a nontrivially normed field κ, a normed ring Y0 with a normed κ-algebra structure, maps f,g:κ→Y0, derivatives a0,b0∈Y0 and z∈κ, HasDerivAt f a0 z and HasDerivAt g b0 z imply HasDerivAt (r↦f(r)g(r)) (a0 g(z)+f(z)b0) z.

hypotheses: κ and Y0 have the stated structures.

output.statement: For every x∈Space and t>0, dot(ubar(x,t),V(x,t))=dot(V(x,t),ubar(x,t))=0 and dot(V(x,t),A(x,t)−L(x,t))=0. The scalar witness in the normality assumption is used only at the current point; no regularity or choice of a witness function is needed.

locals.declaration: Use an arbitrary coordinate k∈Fin m in the component derivative calculation.
Choose a scalar a0 at the current point with A(x,t)−L(x,t)=a0 ubar(x,t), from H005 and the correspondence in N001.

argument.text: Fix arbitrary x and t>0. H004 and the coordinate identification in N001 give ∑_k ubar(x,r)_k²=1 for every r>0, hence on a neighborhood of t. For arbitrary k apply M004 over ℝ to ubar(x,·)_k multiplied by itself; N001 supplies its actual derivative V(x,t)_k. The square has derivative 2 ubar(x,t)_k V(x,t)_k. Differentiating the finite sum gives derivative 2 dot(ubar(x,t),V(x,t)). Since the sum agrees locally with the constant 1, its derivative is zero by locality and uniqueness of derivatives. Division by 2 yields dot(ubar,V)=0; commutativity of real multiplication yields dot(V,ubar)=0. Record F001: these two tangency identities at (x,t).

At this point take just the scalar witness a0 from H005. N001 identifies the original u_tt and Δ_xu with A and L, and u with ubar, so A(x,t)−L(x,t)=a0 ubar(x,t). By finite distributivity of dot and F001, dot(V,A−L)=dot(V,a0 ubar)=a0 dot(V,ubar)=0. Record F002: the required normality cancellation at (x,t). This uses no function selecting scalar witnesses and no derivative of the witness.

Both identities are independent of the chosen scalar's identity. Eliminate that existential choice and universally quantify the arbitrary x and positive t. F001 and F002 prove the exported tangency and cancellation identities. The optional explicit scalar formula and twice-differentiated unit constraint from the original proof are not needed by this authorized route.
